# 1.26.0 — reply to any part of an answer, updates that finish on their own, formulas that render

The main feature of this version: you can now answer a specific passage of an earlier reply —
select it, press **Reply**, and the model knows exactly which words you mean, even if they are from
the very start of a long chat. Around it: updates now install in the background after you close
the window, the chat has arrows to jump to its start and end, formulas written without dollar
signs are finally drawn as formulas, and zoom no longer resets every time you touch something.

Settings, keys and conversations from earlier versions are read as they are.

## Reply to a passage

Long answers usually contain several things you want to react to separately — one step you
disagree with, a command you don't understand, a number that looks wrong. Until now you had to
retype or paste the words yourself and hope the model understood where they came from.

Now select any text in a model's reply — with the mouse or by double-clicking a word — and a small
**Reply** button appears next to the cursor. The same is in the right-click menu and on
**Ctrl + R** (the shortcut can be changed on the **Behavior** page).

- The passage is attached above the input field as a quote with a number: `@1`, `@2`… up to five
  per message.
- In your text you can point at a specific quote by typing `@2`. Typing `@` opens a list of the
  attached quotes: arrows to choose, Enter or Tab to insert. Clicking a quote above the field
  inserts its number too.
- In the sent message the quotes stand as cards above your bubble, and `@N` in the text is
  highlighted. Clicking a card scrolls to the original reply and selects the passage there.

What the model receives is a short, self-explanatory block in front of your message: the quoted
words, and which reply they came from — "your last reply" or "your reply that starts with …". Not
"reply No. 3": the model's own history doesn't count cancelled answers and does count tool rounds,
so a number would point at the wrong place. A very short quote comes with the sentence around it,
so the model knows which of several identical words you mean. Code blocks and formulas survive the
selection intact.

Quotes are kept when you edit the message; if the quoted reply is later deleted, the model is told
so. The "Auto" model choice, chat titles and summaries still read only what you typed yourself.

The right-click menu in the chat is now the program's own — "Copy" and "Reply" in the program's
style instead of the grey system menu with "Cut" and "Paste" that never worked there.

## Updates finish by themselves

- The program checks for a new version at **every launch**, not five hours after the last check.
- If automatic updates are on and a new version was found, closing the window in any way — the
  cross, Alt+F4, the taskbar — hides it at once, and the program quietly finishes the download,
  replaces the file and exits (at most 15 minutes). The download is still verified by size and
  SHA-256.
- If the check at launch failed (no network) or is older than half an hour, closing checks GitHub
  once more, without a window — so what gets installed is what is there now.
- Starting the program again during this work brings the window back; if the file is already being
  replaced, the new version starts right after.
- When Windows shuts down, only an already downloaded update is installed, and without a UAC
  prompt.

## Arrows in the chat

- **To the end** — a round button centred above the input field; it appears when the bottom of
  the chat is far away.
- **To the start** — under the journal button, in its style, when the beginning is far away.

Both glide there with the same physics as the mouse wheel, and the wheel takes over mid-way. On a
short chat there are no arrows at all, and nothing covers the text at the bottom of the chat,
where you spend most of your time.

The chat list and all settings pages can now be scrolled by dragging with the mouse, with inertia
and a rubber-band edge. A click without movement still reaches the button under it.

In the input field, **Up** on the first line moves the caret to the very start of the text and
**Down** on the last line to the very end — as in Discord. The same works when editing your own
message.

## Formulas

- Formulas the model writes **without dollar signs** — bare LaTeX or maths in plain text — are now
  drawn as formulas. Paths, dates, commands and code stay text.
- A slash between simple operands is typeset as a fraction.
- `$|z|$`, `f(x)`, `(x, y)` are no longer shown raw.
- The imaginary unit *i* is upright, and "i sin" no longer runs together into "isin".

## Zoom stays

Zoom used to reset on opening settings, editing, deleting or regenerating a message. Now only
switching to another chat resets it. Editing, deleting and regenerating no longer rebuild the
whole chat — only the changed messages — so it is faster and what you were reading doesn't jump
away. A double click resets zoom only on an empty spot of the chat; on text it selects a word
again.

## Smaller things

- The mouse pointer no longer disappears over the whole program after typing (with Windows'
  "hide pointer while typing" option on).
- "Auto" judges how hard the chat's own answer is, not the work on the PC: that goes to the agent,
  which has its own model choice. A request like "install the driver and check Wi-Fi" no longer
  sends the chat to the flagship model.

## File

`Amarin-Admin-AI-v1.26.0-win-x64.exe` — a single file, nothing to unpack.
